Kylie Cooper | Reuters Macy's on Wednesday announced it's postponing the annual Thanksgiving Day Parade due to severe weather. The parade, held each year on Thursday morning, will now take place on Saturday at 8:30 a.m. ET, according to the company. The New York City area is expected to have heavy rain and thunderstorms on Thanksgiving. "The safety of our participants and spectators is our top priority, and after close consultation with our city and agency partners, we have made the decision to move this year's celebration," Macy's said in a statement. This year's event marks the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade. The annual event has never been canceled due to weather, though it was suspended between 1942 and 1944 for World War II. The parade's viability this year had been in question after concerns arose over strong winds that could become dangerous for the massive balloons that the event is known for. Many of the balloons had already been inflated as of Wednesday afternoon. The postponement also means thousands of volunteers and artists slated to perform will have to adapt to Saturday's schedule. The Technical Committee for Motor Vehicles had been expected to consider, and potentially vote on, the system at its December meeting after no vote was held at two earlier meetings following preliminary approval from the Netherlands in April. Tesla Assisted Driving, renamed from Full Self-Driving as a result of concerns from regulators, is a so-called "hands-off, eyes-on" system that can steer, accelerate and brake while requiring constant supervision from the driver. The vote is a key hurdle in Tesla's effort to roll out the technology across Europe. Nearly a dozen countries have followed the Dutch lead, with Italy the most populous to begin a rollout. But EU-wide approval requires backing from at least 15 of the bloc's 27 member states representing 65% of its population. A rejection at EU level would invalidate the national approvals already granted. The meeting had originally been scheduled for Dec. 1, Dutch regulator RDW told Reuters.
